title: Automatic Clipping: Differentially Private Deep Learning Made Easier and Stronger

en.text: Training a neural network with a differential-privacy (DP) guarantee follows a well-worn recipe. For each example in a batch you compute its own gradient, rescale that gradient so its norm never exceeds a fixed threshold R, add Gaussian noise calibrated to R, and only then take an optimizer step. This per-sample clipping is what bounds any single example's influence on the model, and it is what makes the privacy accounting go through. It also introduces R, a hyperparameter that turns out to be one of the most consequential and least forgiving choices in the entire pipeline.

The trouble is that R behaves nothing like a gentle knob. Set it a little too high and the noise, which scales with R, drowns the signal; set it too low and every gradient is squashed to the same tiny norm. Because the right value is task- and model-specific, practitioners end up searching jointly over R and the learning rate, a two-dimensional grid that, for large models, can take days to months of compute. Worse, that search reads the private training data, so it quietly spends extra privacy budget on top of the training itself.

This paper, "Automatic Clipping: Differentially Private Deep Learning Made Easier and Stronger" from AWS AI and UC Santa Barbara, makes a clean claim: R does not need to be tuned, because it does not need to exist. The authors show the threshold can be removed from any DP optimizer with essentially a one-line code change, yielding a method that is just as private, just as fast, and at least as accurate as the best hand-tuned baselines, with a convergence guarantee that matches ordinary SGD.
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.07136   |   Code: https://github.com/awslabs/fast-differential-privacy
Why the clipping threshold is such a headache

Standard DP-SGD, following Abadi et al., clips each per-sample gradient g by the factor min(R / ‖g‖, 1): gradients longer than R are scaled down to length R, and shorter ones are left alone. In practice, though, the thresholds that give the best accuracy are tiny, small enough that essentially every per-sample gradient is longer than R and therefore gets clipped at every step. When that happens the min collapses to its first branch, R / ‖g‖, for almost every example. The exact value of R stops carrying any per-example magnitude information; it acts only as a global scale. That observation is the crack the paper pries open.

en.caption: Figure 1. Test accuracy of ResNet18 on ImageNet under DP-SGD, swept over the clipping norm (x-axis) and learning rate (y-axis). Accuracy runs from about 60% at a good configuration down to single digits, and even along a strong learning-rate row it falls sharply once the clipping norm is set too large. The threshold, not just the learning rate, decides the outcome.

en.text: From a threshold to a normalization: AUTO-V

If nearly every gradient is being scaled by R / ‖g‖ anyway, why keep the min at all? Automatic clipping drops it and applies the normalization to every gradient unconditionally. The paper calls this vanilla variant AUTO-V:
Clip_AUTO-V(g; R) = R / ‖g‖ .

Normalizing every gradient to the same length has a concrete benefit: it maximizes the alignment between the aggregated private gradient and the true gradient, because no single large example can dominate the sum. Figure 2 makes this visible. The per-step dot product between the private and true gradient stays markedly higher for AUTO-V than for Abadi's clipping throughout training.

en.caption: Figure 2. Per-step dot-product similarity between the private (clipped, noised) gradient and the true gradient over training. AUTO-V normalization (blue) keeps the private gradient far more aligned with the true gradient than Abadi's clipping (orange), which is the intuition behind dropping the threshold and simply normalizing.

en.text: But pure normalization overshoots. If every gradient is forced to the same magnitude, then small gradients, the ones near a good solution where you want the updates to shrink, are inflated back to full size. Training enters a "lazy region" where it can no longer settle, and AUTO-V on its own can fail to converge.
Restoring magnitude: AUTO-S and the disappearing threshold

The fix is small and surgical. Instead of dividing by ‖g‖, AUTO-S divides by ‖g‖ + γ for a small positive stability constant γ: Clip_AUTO-S(g; R) = R / (‖g‖ + γ). For a large gradient the γ is negligible and AUTO-S behaves like AUTO-V; but as a gradient shrinks toward zero, the clipped result approaches g / γ rather than a fixed length, so small gradients stay small. That single term restores the magnitude information the normalization threw away, and it is what lets the method converge all the way to a zero-gradient solution.

The last step is where the threshold actually disappears. Multiplying every clipped gradient by a constant R is mathematically identical to leaving R at 1 and scaling the learning rate instead, and the noise scale rides along with it, so the privacy guarantee is untouched. The authors therefore simply fix R = 1. What remains is an optimizer with no clipping threshold to choose: one default stability constant (the paper uses γ = 0.01) replaces an entire axis of the hyperparameter grid, and the same substitution drops into DP-SGD, DP-Adam, or DP-LAMB, and into existing libraries such as Opacus, by swapping a single clipping function.
Does deleting the knob cost accuracy? No.

The central experiment asks whether a fixed, threshold-free rule can really match a carefully tuned R. Figure 3 answers it directly. Each heatmap cell is the SST-2 test accuracy of RoBERTa-base at ε = 3 for a given (clipping norm, learning rate) pair; the extra AUTO-S column on the right uses no tuned threshold at all. It lands on the same accuracy as the best hand-tuned R, which means you can search the learning rate alone and skip the R axis entirely, cutting the tuning cost roughly 5 times (and in the privacy budget that tuning would spend).

en.caption: Figure 3. RoBERTa-base test accuracy on SST-2 (DP-Adam, ε = 3) across clipping thresholds R and learning rates. The AUTO-S column past the red line uses no tuned threshold, yet reaches the same accuracy as the best hand-tuned R; searching only the learning rate shrinks the hyperparameter grid to about a fifth.

en.text: The pattern holds across tasks, and often the gap is not just "matched" but clearly better. On image benchmarks AUTO-S improves over Abadi's clipping at the same privacy budget on every task the paper reports, with the largest jumps where accuracy has the most room to move.

en.caption: Table 1. AUTO-S versus the tuned baseline at matched privacy budget ε. Numbers are test accuracy (%); higher is better.

en.text: The language results tell the same story. On the GLUE tasks with RoBERTa, AUTO-S matches or beats the previous best DP fine-tuning numbers, and on E2E table-to-text generation with GPT2 it reaches a BLEU of 64.18 (GPT2-large, ε = 3), at the top of the reported models. The recurring theme is that the method never needs a tuned threshold to get there.
Why it works, not just that it works

Automatic clipping is not only an empirical trick; the paper proves it converges. For non-convex objectives, automatic DP-SGD with AUTO-S drives the minimum expected gradient norm down at the rate O(T^{-1/4}) in the number of steps T, the same asymptotic rate as standard, non-private SGD. Figure 4 traces the upper bound on that quantity across several values of a gradient-asymmetry ratio r, and every curve settles onto the standard-SGD slope. The analysis also shows the method is essentially insensitive to γ: any positive value yields the same asymptotic rate, which is what justifies shipping a single default instead of yet another thing to tune.

en.caption: Figure 4. Convergence of automatic DP-SGD (AUTO-S): the upper bound on min_t E‖g_t‖ against the number of iterations T on a log-log scale, for several values of the gradient-asymmetry ratio r. Every curve flattens at the standard-SGD rate O(T^{-1/4}), so removing the threshold costs nothing asymptotically.

en.text: Takeaway

The clipping threshold has been treated as a critical, must-tune knob since DP deep learning began. The message of automatic clipping is that it can simply be removed: normalize each per-sample gradient, add a tiny stability constant, fix the threshold to one, and you are left with an optimizer that is as private, as fast, and as accurate as the best hand-tuned DP methods, backed by a convergence guarantee matching SGD. The honest boundary is that automatic clipping changes how gradients are clipped, not the underlying privacy-utility trade-off of DP itself: noise still has to be added, and very tight privacy budgets are still hard. What it removes is a large, expensive, and largely unnecessary source of friction, which is enough to make private training feel a lot more like ordinary training.

Because the change is a drop-in replacement for the clipping step, it costs almost nothing to try: the authors release it in the open-source fast-differential-privacy library, where switching an existing DP-Adam or DP-SGD run to automatic clipping means swapping one function and deleting the threshold from the search. For most practitioners, that turns a two-dimensional hyperparameter hunt into a one-dimensional one, with no measured cost in accuracy or privacy.

zh.text: 给神经网络加上差分隐私（differential privacy, DP）保证，通常遵循一套固定流程：对一个 batch 里的每个样本单独求梯度，把该梯度的范数缩放到不超过某个固定阈值 R，再按 R 校准加入高斯噪声，最后才更新参数。这一步“逐样本梯度裁剪”（per-sample gradient clipping）既限制了任何单个样本对模型的影响，也是隐私核算能够成立的前提。但它同时引入了一个超参数 R，而这个 R，恰恰是整条流程里最关键、也最不容出错的选择之一。
麻烦在于，R 完全不是一个“温和”的旋钮。设得偏大，随 R 一同放大的噪声会淹没真实梯度；设得偏小，所有梯度又会被压成同样的极小范数。由于最优取值和任务、模型强相关，实践中人们只能在 R 和学习率上做联合网格搜索：对大模型而言，这样一轮二维搜索动辄需要几天到几个月的算力。更棘手的是，这个搜索过程会读取隐私训练数据，因此还会在训练本身之外，悄悄多花掉一部分隐私预算。

这篇来自 AWS AI 与 UC Santa Barbara 的论文《Automatic Clipping: Differentially Private Deep Learning Made Easier and Stronger》，给出的判断很干脆：R 不需要调，因为它根本不需要存在。作者证明，几乎只用改一行代码，就能把裁剪阈值从任意 DP 优化器中移除，得到一个同样私密、同样高效、精度追平甚至超过最优精调基线的方法，并且带有和普通 SGD 相同的收敛保证。
论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.07136   |   代码：https://github.com/awslabs/fast-differential-privacy
为什么裁剪阈值这么让人头疼

标准的 DP-SGD 沿用 Abadi 等人的做法，用系数 min(R / ‖g‖, 1) 裁剪每个逐样本梯度 g：范数超过 R 的梯度被缩放到长度 R，没超过的保持不变。但在实践中，能带来最好精度的阈值往往非常小，小到几乎每个逐样本梯度都比 R 长，于是每一步、每个样本都会被裁剪。这时 min 几乎总是取到前一支 R / ‖g‖，R 的具体数值不再携带任何逐样本的幅度信息，只相当于一个全局缩放系数。论文正是从这个观察撬开了缺口。

zh.caption: 图1 ImageNet 上 ResNet18 在 DP-SGD 下的测试准确率，横轴为裁剪范数（clipping norm），纵轴为学习率。准确率在好的配置下约为 60%，在差的配置下会跌到个位数；即便沿着一条不错的学习率取值，一旦把裁剪范数调得过大，准确率也会明显下滑。决定成败的不只是学习率，还有这个阈值本身。

zh.text: 从阈值到归一化：AUTO-V
既然几乎每个梯度反正都在乘 R / ‖g‖，那还留着这个 min 干什么？自动裁剪干脆把它去掉，对所有梯度无条件地做这一步归一化。作者把这个朴素版本称为 AUTO-V（vanilla）：
Clip_AUTO-V(g; R) = R / ‖g‖ 。
把每个梯度都归一化到相同长度有一个实在的好处：它让聚合后的私有梯度与真实梯度的方向尽可能一致，因为不再有某个大梯度样本主导整个求和。图2 把这一点直接画了出来：训练全过程中，AUTO-V 的私有梯度与真实梯度之间的逐步点积，明显高于 Abadi 裁剪。

zh.caption: 图2 每一步中，私有（裁剪并加噪后）梯度与真实梯度之间的点积相似度。AUTO-V 归一化（蓝色）让私有梯度与真实梯度的对齐程度远高于 Abadi 裁剪（橙色），这正是“去掉阈值、直接归一化”背后的直觉。

zh.text: 但纯归一化用力过猛。如果强行把每个梯度都拉到同样的幅度，那些本该变小的小梯度（出现在接近好解的区域、我们希望更新随之收缩的地方）就会被重新放大回原来的大小。训练由此进入一个“惰性区”（lazy region），迟迟无法稳定下来，单靠 AUTO-V 可能无法收敛。
把幅度找回来：AUTO-S，以及消失的阈值

修法很小，也很精准。AUTO-S 不再除以 ‖g‖，而是除以 ‖g‖ + γ，其中 γ 是一个很小的正稳定常数：Clip_AUTO-S(g; R) = R / (‖g‖ + γ)。对大梯度来说 γ 可以忽略，AUTO-S 表现得和 AUTO-V 一致；但当梯度趋近于零，裁剪结果趋向 g / γ 而不是某个固定长度，于是小梯度依然是小梯度。这一项把归一化丢掉的幅度信息重新补了回来，也正是它让方法能够一路收敛到梯度范数为零的解。

最后一步，才是阈值真正消失的地方。给每个裁剪后的梯度都乘上常数 R，在数学上等价于把 R 固定为 1、转而缩放学习率，而噪声尺度会一起跟着走，因此隐私保证丝毫不受影响。于是作者索性令 R = 1。剩下的，就是一个没有裁剪阈值需要选的优化器：一个默认的稳定常数（论文取 γ = 0.01）替代了整整一个维度的超参搜索。同样的替换可以直接套进 DP-SGD、DP-Adam 或 DP-LAMB，也能通过替换一个裁剪函数嵌入 Opacus 等现有库。
删掉这个旋钮，会牺牲精度吗？不会

最核心的实验，就是要回答一个固定的、无阈值的规则能否真的追平精调过的 R。图3 给出了直接的答案。热力图里每个格子是 RoBERTa-base 在 SST-2、ε = 3 下、某个（裁剪范数，学习率）组合的测试准确率；右侧多出来的 AUTO-S 一列则完全不使用任何调过的阈值。它落在了与最优精调 R 相同的准确率上，也就是说，你只需搜索学习率，整条 R 维度可以直接跳过，调参成本大约省下 5 倍（连同这部分调参本会花掉的隐私预算）。

zh.caption: 图3 RoBERTa-base 在 SST-2 上的测试准确率（DP-Adam，ε = 3），横轴为裁剪阈值 R，纵轴为学习率。红线右侧的 AUTO-S 一列不调阈值，却达到了与最优精调 R 相同的准确率；只搜索学习率，就能把超参网格大约缩小到原来的五分之一。

zh.text: 这个规律在各类任务上都成立，而且往往不只是“追平”，而是明显更好。在图像基准上，相同隐私预算下，AUTO-S 在论文报告的每一个任务上都超过了 Abadi 裁剪，提升最大的地方，正是准确率本来最有空间的任务。

zh.caption: 表1 相同隐私预算 ε 下，AUTO-S 与精调基线的对比。数值为测试准确率（%），越高越好。

zh.text: 语言任务上的结论如出一辙。在 GLUE 的 RoBERTa 微调上，AUTO-S 追平或超过了此前最好的 DP 微调结果；在 GPT2 的 E2E 表格到文本生成上，它拿到了 64.18 的 BLEU（GPT2-large，ε = 3），位居所报告模型的前列。反复出现的主题是：达到这些成绩，方法从不需要一个调过的阈值。
不仅有效，而且讲得清为什么有效

自动裁剪并不只是一个经验技巧，论文还证明了它会收敛。在非凸目标下，采用 AUTO-S 的自动 DP-SGD 能让最小期望梯度范数以 O(T^{-1/4}) 的速率随步数 T 下降，这与标准的、非私有的 SGD 的渐近速率完全相同。图4 画出了这个上界在若干“梯度不对称比” r 取值下随 T 的变化，每条曲线最终都落到了标准 SGD 的斜率上。分析还表明，方法对 γ 基本不敏感：任何正值都给出相同的渐近速率，这正是“发一个默认值即可、不必再多调一个超参”的理由。

zh.caption: 图4 采用 AUTO-S 的自动 DP-SGD 的收敛情况：纵轴为 min_t E‖g_t‖ 的上界，横轴为迭代步数 T，双对数坐标，对应若干“梯度不对称比” r 的取值。每条曲线最终都以标准 SGD 的速率 O(T^{-1/4}) 趋于平缓，说明去掉阈值在渐近意义上不付出任何代价。

zh.text: 小结

自差分隐私深度学习诞生以来，裁剪阈值一直被当作一个必须仔细调的关键旋钮。自动裁剪想说的是：它其实可以被直接删掉。把每个逐样本梯度归一化，加上一个很小的稳定常数，再把阈值固定为 1，你就得到了一个和最优精调 DP 方法同样私密、同样高效、同样准确的优化器，还附带与 SGD 相同的收敛保证。需要诚实说明的边界是：自动裁剪改变的是“梯度怎么裁剪”，而不是差分隐私本身的隐私-效用权衡，噪声该加还得加，极紧的隐私预算依然困难。但它去掉的，是一处庞大、昂贵、且在很大程度上并不必要的摩擦，这已经足以让私有训练用起来更接近普通训练。
由于这一改动只是裁剪步骤的即插即用替换，尝试它的成本几乎为零：作者已将其开源在 fast-differential-privacy 库中，把现有的 DP-Adam 或 DP-SGD 训练切换到自动裁剪，只需替换一个函数、并从搜索空间里删掉阈值这一维。对多数使用者而言，这把原本二维的超参搜索变成了一维，而在精度和隐私上都没有可测量的代价。

en.text: Why the clipping threshold is such a headache

Standard DP-SGD, following Abadi et al., clips each per-sample gradient g by the factor min(R / ‖g‖, 1): gradients longer than R are scaled down to length R, and shorter ones are left alone. In practice, though, the thresholds that give the best accuracy are tiny, small enough that essentially every per-sample gradient is longer than R and therefore gets clipped at every step. When that happens the min collapses to its first branch, R / ‖g‖, for almost every example. The exact value of R stops carrying any per-example magnitude information; it acts only as a global scale. That observation is the crack the paper pries open.

en.caption: Figure 1. Test accuracy of ResNet18 on ImageNet under DP-SGD, swept over the clipping norm (x-axis) and learning rate (y-axis). Accuracy runs from about 60% at a good configuration down to single digits, and even along a strong learning-rate row it falls sharply once the clipping norm is set too large. The threshold, not just the learning rate, decides the outcome.

zh.text: 为什么裁剪阈值这么让人头疼

标准的 DP-SGD 沿用 Abadi 等人的做法，用系数 min(R / ‖g‖, 1) 裁剪每个逐样本梯度 g：范数超过 R 的梯度被缩放到长度 R，没超过的保持不变。但在实践中，能带来最好精度的阈值往往非常小，小到几乎每个逐样本梯度都比 R 长，于是每一步、每个样本都会被裁剪。这时 min 几乎总是取到前一支 R / ‖g‖，R 的具体数值不再携带任何逐样本的幅度信息，只相当于一个全局缩放系数。论文正是从这个观察撬开了缺口。

zh.caption: 图1 ImageNet 上 ResNet18 在 DP-SGD 下的测试准确率，横轴为裁剪范数（clipping norm），纵轴为学习率。准确率在好的配置下约为 60%，在差的配置下会跌到个位数；即便沿着一条不错的学习率取值，一旦把裁剪范数调得过大，准确率也会明显下滑。决定成败的不只是学习率，还有这个阈值本身。

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 差分隐私训练里最难调的那个旋钮，其实可以删掉
zh.subtitle: AWS AI 与 UC Santa Barbara 提出自动裁剪（automatic clipping）：一行代码去掉裁剪阈值，效果追平甚至超过精调后的最优基线。

en.text: From a threshold to a normalization: AUTO-V

If nearly every gradient is being scaled by R / ‖g‖ anyway, why keep the min at all? Automatic clipping drops it and applies the normalization to every gradient unconditionally. The paper calls this vanilla variant AUTO-V:
Clip_AUTO-V(g; R) = R / ‖g‖ .

Normalizing every gradient to the same length has a concrete benefit: it maximizes the alignment between the aggregated private gradient and the true gradient, because no single large example can dominate the sum. Figure 2 makes this visible. The per-step dot product between the private and true gradient stays markedly higher for AUTO-V than for Abadi's clipping throughout training.

en.caption: Figure 2. Per-step dot-product similarity between the private (clipped, noised) gradient and the true gradient over training. AUTO-V normalization (blue) keeps the private gradient far more aligned with the true gradient than Abadi's clipping (orange), which is the intuition behind dropping the threshold and simply normalizing.

en.text: But pure normalization overshoots. If every gradient is forced to the same magnitude, then small gradients, the ones near a good solution where you want the updates to shrink, are inflated back to full size. Training enters a "lazy region" where it can no longer settle, and AUTO-V on its own can fail to converge.

zh.text: 从阈值到归一化：AUTO-V
既然几乎每个梯度反正都在乘 R / ‖g‖，那还留着这个 min 干什么？自动裁剪干脆把它去掉，对所有梯度无条件地做这一步归一化。作者把这个朴素版本称为 AUTO-V（vanilla）：
Clip_AUTO-V(g; R) = R / ‖g‖ 。
把每个梯度都归一化到相同长度有一个实在的好处：它让聚合后的私有梯度与真实梯度的方向尽可能一致，因为不再有某个大梯度样本主导整个求和。图2 把这一点直接画了出来：训练全过程中，AUTO-V 的私有梯度与真实梯度之间的逐步点积，明显高于 Abadi 裁剪。

zh.caption: 图2 每一步中，私有（裁剪并加噪后）梯度与真实梯度之间的点积相似度。AUTO-V 归一化（蓝色）让私有梯度与真实梯度的对齐程度远高于 Abadi 裁剪（橙色），这正是“去掉阈值、直接归一化”背后的直觉。

zh.text: 但纯归一化用力过猛。如果强行把每个梯度都拉到同样的幅度，那些本该变小的小梯度（出现在接近好解的区域、我们希望更新随之收缩的地方）就会被重新放大回原来的大小。训练由此进入一个“惰性区”（lazy region），迟迟无法稳定下来，单靠 AUTO-V 可能无法收敛。

en.title: NeurIPS 2023 | Removing the Trickiest Knob in Private Deep Learning
en.subtitle: AWS AI and UC Santa Barbara introduce automatic clipping: a one-line replacement that deletes the clipping threshold from any DP optimizer while matching or beating tuned state of the art.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 差分隐私训练里最难调的那个旋钮，其实可以删掉
zh.subtitle: AWS AI 与 UC Santa Barbara 提出自动裁剪（automatic clipping）：一行代码去掉裁剪阈值，效果追平甚至超过精调后的最优基线。

en.caption: Figure 3. RoBERTa-base test accuracy on SST-2 (DP-Adam, ε = 3) across clipping thresholds R and learning rates. The AUTO-S column past the red line uses no tuned threshold, yet reaches the same accuracy as the best hand-tuned R; searching only the learning rate shrinks the hyperparameter grid to about a fifth.

en.text: Training a neural network with a differential-privacy (DP) guarantee follows a well-worn recipe. For each example in a batch you compute its own gradient, rescale that gradient so its norm never exceeds a fixed threshold R, add Gaussian noise calibrated to R, and only then take an optimizer step. This per-sample clipping is what bounds any single example's influence on the model, and it is what makes the privacy accounting go through. It also introduces R, a hyperparameter that turns out to be one of the most consequential and least forgiving choices in the entire pipeline.

The trouble is that R behaves nothing like a gentle knob. Set it a little too high and the noise, which scales with R, drowns the signal; set it too low and every gradient is squashed to the same tiny norm. Because the right value is task- and model-specific, practitioners end up searching jointly over R and the learning rate, a two-dimensional grid that, for large models, can take days to months of compute. Worse, that search reads the private training data, so it quietly spends extra privacy budget on top of the training itself.

This paper, "Automatic Clipping: Differentially Private Deep Learning Made Easier and Stronger" from AWS AI and UC Santa Barbara, makes a clean claim: R does not need to be tuned, because it does not need to exist. The authors show the threshold can be removed from any DP optimizer with essentially a one-line code change, yielding a method that is just as private, just as fast, and at least as accurate as the best hand-tuned baselines, with a convergence guarantee that matches ordinary SGD.
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.07136   |   Code: https://github.com/awslabs/fast-differential-privacy
Takeaway

The clipping threshold has been treated as a critical, must-tune knob since DP deep learning began. The message of automatic clipping is that it can simply be removed: normalize each per-sample gradient, add a tiny stability constant, fix the threshold to one, and you are left with an optimizer that is as private, as fast, and as accurate as the best hand-tuned DP methods, backed by a convergence guarantee matching SGD. The honest boundary is that automatic clipping changes how gradients are clipped, not the underlying privacy-utility trade-off of DP itself: noise still has to be added, and very tight privacy budgets are still hard. What it removes is a large, expensive, and largely unnecessary source of friction, which is enough to make private training feel a lot more like ordinary training.

Because the change is a drop-in replacement for the clipping step, it costs almost nothing to try: the authors release it in the open-source fast-differential-privacy library, where switching an existing DP-Adam or DP-SGD run to automatic clipping means swapping one function and deleting the threshold from the search. For most practitioners, that turns a two-dimensional hyperparameter hunt into a one-dimensional one, with no measured cost in accuracy or privacy.

zh.caption: 图3 RoBERTa-base 在 SST-2 上的测试准确率（DP-Adam，ε = 3），横轴为裁剪阈值 R，纵轴为学习率。红线右侧的 AUTO-S 一列不调阈值，却达到了与最优精调 R 相同的准确率；只搜索学习率，就能把超参网格大约缩小到原来的五分之一。

zh.text: 给神经网络加上差分隐私（differential privacy, DP）保证，通常遵循一套固定流程：对一个 batch 里的每个样本单独求梯度，把该梯度的范数缩放到不超过某个固定阈值 R，再按 R 校准加入高斯噪声，最后才更新参数。这一步“逐样本梯度裁剪”（per-sample gradient clipping）既限制了任何单个样本对模型的影响，也是隐私核算能够成立的前提。但它同时引入了一个超参数 R，而这个 R，恰恰是整条流程里最关键、也最不容出错的选择之一。
麻烦在于，R 完全不是一个“温和”的旋钮。设得偏大，随 R 一同放大的噪声会淹没真实梯度；设得偏小，所有梯度又会被压成同样的极小范数。由于最优取值和任务、模型强相关，实践中人们只能在 R 和学习率上做联合网格搜索：对大模型而言，这样一轮二维搜索动辄需要几天到几个月的算力。更棘手的是，这个搜索过程会读取隐私训练数据，因此还会在训练本身之外，悄悄多花掉一部分隐私预算。

这篇来自 AWS AI 与 UC Santa Barbara 的论文《Automatic Clipping: Differentially Private Deep Learning Made Easier and Stronger》，给出的判断很干脆：R 不需要调，因为它根本不需要存在。作者证明，几乎只用改一行代码，就能把裁剪阈值从任意 DP 优化器中移除，得到一个同样私密、同样高效、精度追平甚至超过最优精调基线的方法，并且带有和普通 SGD 相同的收敛保证。
论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.07136   |   代码：https://github.com/awslabs/fast-differential-privacy
把幅度找回来：AUTO-S，以及消失的阈值

修法很小，也很精准。AUTO-S 不再除以 ‖g‖，而是除以 ‖g‖ + γ，其中 γ 是一个很小的正稳定常数：Clip_AUTO-S(g; R) = R / (‖g‖ + γ)。对大梯度来说 γ 可以忽略，AUTO-S 表现得和 AUTO-V 一致；但当梯度趋近于零，裁剪结果趋向 g / γ 而不是某个固定长度，于是小梯度依然是小梯度。这一项把归一化丢掉的幅度信息重新补了回来，也正是它让方法能够一路收敛到梯度范数为零的解。

最后一步，才是阈值真正消失的地方。给每个裁剪后的梯度都乘上常数 R，在数学上等价于把 R 固定为 1、转而缩放学习率，而噪声尺度会一起跟着走，因此隐私保证丝毫不受影响。于是作者索性令 R = 1。剩下的，就是一个没有裁剪阈值需要选的优化器：一个默认的稳定常数（论文取 γ = 0.01）替代了整整一个维度的超参搜索。同样的替换可以直接套进 DP-SGD、DP-Adam 或 DP-LAMB，也能通过替换一个裁剪函数嵌入 Opacus 等现有库。

en.title: NeurIPS 2023 | Removing the Trickiest Knob in Private Deep Learning
en.subtitle: AWS AI and UC Santa Barbara introduce automatic clipping: a one-line replacement that deletes the clipping threshold from any DP optimizer while matching or beating tuned state of the art.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 差分隐私训练里最难调的那个旋钮，其实可以删掉
zh.subtitle: AWS AI 与 UC Santa Barbara 提出自动裁剪（automatic clipping）：一行代码去掉裁剪阈值，效果追平甚至超过精调后的最优基线。

en.text: Does deleting the knob cost accuracy? No.

The central experiment asks whether a fixed, threshold-free rule can really match a carefully tuned R. Figure 3 answers it directly. Each heatmap cell is the SST-2 test accuracy of RoBERTa-base at ε = 3 for a given (clipping norm, learning rate) pair; the extra AUTO-S column on the right uses no tuned threshold at all. It lands on the same accuracy as the best hand-tuned R, which means you can search the learning rate alone and skip the R axis entirely, cutting the tuning cost roughly 5 times (and in the privacy budget that tuning would spend).

en.caption: Figure 3. RoBERTa-base test accuracy on SST-2 (DP-Adam, ε = 3) across clipping thresholds R and learning rates. The AUTO-S column past the red line uses no tuned threshold, yet reaches the same accuracy as the best hand-tuned R; searching only the learning rate shrinks the hyperparameter grid to about a fifth.

en.text: The pattern holds across tasks, and often the gap is not just "matched" but clearly better. On image benchmarks AUTO-S improves over Abadi's clipping at the same privacy budget on every task the paper reports, with the largest jumps where accuracy has the most room to move.

en.caption: Table 1. AUTO-S versus the tuned baseline at matched privacy budget ε. Numbers are test accuracy (%); higher is better.

en.text: The language results tell the same story. On the GLUE tasks with RoBERTa, AUTO-S matches or beats the previous best DP fine-tuning numbers, and on E2E table-to-text generation with GPT2 it reaches a BLEU of 64.18 (GPT2-large, ε = 3), at the top of the reported models. The recurring theme is that the method never needs a tuned threshold to get there.

zh.text: 删掉这个旋钮，会牺牲精度吗？不会

最核心的实验，就是要回答一个固定的、无阈值的规则能否真的追平精调过的 R。图3 给出了直接的答案。热力图里每个格子是 RoBERTa-base 在 SST-2、ε = 3 下、某个（裁剪范数，学习率）组合的测试准确率；右侧多出来的 AUTO-S 一列则完全不使用任何调过的阈值。它落在了与最优精调 R 相同的准确率上，也就是说，你只需搜索学习率，整条 R 维度可以直接跳过，调参成本大约省下 5 倍（连同这部分调参本会花掉的隐私预算）。

zh.caption: 图3 RoBERTa-base 在 SST-2 上的测试准确率（DP-Adam，ε = 3），横轴为裁剪阈值 R，纵轴为学习率。红线右侧的 AUTO-S 一列不调阈值，却达到了与最优精调 R 相同的准确率；只搜索学习率，就能把超参网格大约缩小到原来的五分之一。

zh.text: 这个规律在各类任务上都成立，而且往往不只是“追平”，而是明显更好。在图像基准上，相同隐私预算下，AUTO-S 在论文报告的每一个任务上都超过了 Abadi 裁剪，提升最大的地方，正是准确率本来最有空间的任务。

zh.caption: 表1 相同隐私预算 ε 下，AUTO-S 与精调基线的对比。数值为测试准确率（%），越高越好。

zh.text: 语言任务上的结论如出一辙。在 GLUE 的 RoBERTa 微调上，AUTO-S 追平或超过了此前最好的 DP 微调结果；在 GPT2 的 E2E 表格到文本生成上，它拿到了 64.18 的 BLEU（GPT2-large，ε = 3），位居所报告模型的前列。反复出现的主题是：达到这些成绩，方法从不需要一个调过的阈值。

The fix is small and surgical. Instead of dividing by ‖g‖, AUTO-S divides by ‖g‖ + γ for a small positive stability constant γ: Clip_AUTO-S(g; R) = R / (‖g‖ + γ). The last step is where the threshold actually disappears. Standard DP-SGD, following Abadi et al., clips each per-sample gradient g by the factor min(R / ‖g‖, 1): gradients longer than R are scaled down to length R, and shorter ones are left alone. In practice, though, the thresholds that give the best accuracy are tiny, small enough that essentially every per-sample gradient is longer than R and therefore gets clipped at every step. When that happens the min collapses to its first branch, R / ‖g‖, for almost every example. The exact value of R stops carrying any per-example magnitude information; it acts only as a global scale. That observation is the crack the paper pries open.

en.caption: Figure 1. Test accuracy of ResNet18 on ImageNet under DP-SGD, swept over the clipping norm (x-axis) and learning rate (y-axis). Accuracy runs from about 60% at a good configuration down to single digits, and even along a strong learning-rate row it falls sharply once the clipping norm is set too large. The threshold, not just the learning rate, decides the outcome.

zh.caption: 图4 采用 AUTO-S 的自动 DP-SGD 的收敛情况：纵轴为 min_t E‖g_t‖ 的上界，横轴为迭代步数 T，双对数坐标，对应若干“梯度不对称比” r 的取值。每条曲线最终都以标准 SGD 的速率 O(T^{-1/4}) 趋于平缓，说明去掉阈值在渐近意义上不付出任何代价。

zh.text: 给神经网络加上差分隐私（differential privacy, DP）保证，通常遵循一套固定流程：对一个 batch 里的每个样本单独求梯度，把该梯度的范数缩放到不超过某个固定阈值 R，再按 R 校准加入高斯噪声，最后才更新参数。这一步“逐样本梯度裁剪”（per-sample gradient clipping）既限制了任何单个样本对模型的影响，也是隐私核算能够成立的前提。但它同时引入了一个超参数 R，而这个 R，恰恰是整条流程里最关键、也最不容出错的选择之一。
麻烦在于，R 完全不是一个“温和”的旋钮。设得偏大，随 R 一同放大的噪声会淹没真实梯度；设得偏小，所有梯度又会被压成同样的极小范数。由于最优取值和任务、模型强相关，实践中人们只能在 R 和学习率上做联合网格搜索：对大模型而言，这样一轮二维搜索动辄需要几天到几个月的算力。更棘手的是，这个搜索过程会读取隐私训练数据，因此还会在训练本身之外，悄悄多花掉一部分隐私预算。

这篇来自 AWS AI 与 UC Santa Barbara 的论文《Automatic Clipping: Differentially Private Deep Learning Made Easier and Stronger》，给出的判断很干脆：R 不需要调，因为它根本不需要存在。作者证明，几乎只用改一行代码，就能把裁剪阈值从任意 DP 优化器中移除，得到一个同样私密、同样高效、精度追平甚至超过最优精调基线的方法，并且带有和普通 SGD 相同的收敛保证。
论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.07136   |   代码：https://github.com/awslabs/fast-differential-privacy

en.title: NeurIPS 2023 | Removing the Trickiest Knob in Private Deep Learning
en.subtitle: AWS AI and UC Santa Barbara introduce automatic clipping: a one-line replacement that deletes the clipping threshold from any DP optimizer while matching or beating tuned state of the art.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 差分隐私训练里最难调的那个旋钮，其实可以删掉
zh.subtitle: AWS AI 与 UC Santa Barbara 提出自动裁剪（automatic clipping）：一行代码去掉裁剪阈值，效果追平甚至超过精调后的最优基线。

en.text: Does deleting the knob cost accuracy? No.

The central experiment asks whether a fixed, threshold-free rule can really match a carefully tuned R. Figure 3 answers it directly. Each heatmap cell is the SST-2 test accuracy of RoBERTa-base at ε = 3 for a given (clipping norm, learning rate) pair; the extra AUTO-S column on the right uses no tuned threshold at all. It lands on the same accuracy as the best hand-tuned R, which means you can search the learning rate alone and skip the R axis entirely, cutting the tuning cost roughly 5 times (and in the privacy budget that tuning would spend).

en.caption: Figure 3. RoBERTa-base test accuracy on SST-2 (DP-Adam, ε = 3) across clipping thresholds R and learning rates. The AUTO-S column past the red line uses no tuned threshold, yet reaches the same accuracy as the best hand-tuned R; searching only the learning rate shrinks the hyperparameter grid to about a fifth.

en.text: The pattern holds across tasks, and often the gap is not just "matched" but clearly better. On image benchmarks AUTO-S improves over Abadi's clipping at the same privacy budget on every task the paper reports, with the largest jumps where accuracy has the most room to move.

en.caption: Table 1. AUTO-S versus the tuned baseline at matched privacy budget ε. Numbers are test accuracy (%); higher is better.

en.text: The language results tell the same story. On the GLUE tasks with RoBERTa, AUTO-S matches or beats the previous best DP fine-tuning numbers, and on E2E table-to-text generation with GPT2 it reaches a BLEU of 64.18 (GPT2-large, ε = 3), at the top of the reported models. The recurring theme is that the method never needs a tuned threshold to get there.

zh.caption: 图1 ImageNet 上 ResNet18 在 DP-SGD 下的测试准确率，横轴为裁剪范数（clipping norm），纵轴为学习率。准确率在好的配置下约为 60%，在差的配置下会跌到个位数；即便沿着一条不错的学习率取值，一旦把裁剪范数调得过大，准确率也会明显下滑。决定成败的不只是学习率，还有这个阈值本身。

zh.text: 小结

自差分隐私深度学习诞生以来，裁剪阈值一直被当作一个必须仔细调的关键旋钮。自动裁剪想说的是：它其实可以被直接删掉。把每个逐样本梯度归一化，加上一个很小的稳定常数，再把阈值固定为 1，你就得到了一个和最优精调 DP 方法同样私密、同样高效、同样准确的优化器，还附带与 SGD 相同的收敛保证。需要诚实说明的边界是：自动裁剪改变的是“梯度怎么裁剪”，而不是差分隐私本身的隐私-效用权衡，噪声该加还得加，极紧的隐私预算依然困难。但它去掉的，是一处庞大、昂贵、且在很大程度上并不必要的摩擦，这已经足以让私有训练用起来更接近普通训练。
由于这一改动只是裁剪步骤的即插即用替换，尝试它的成本几乎为零：作者已将其开源在 fast-differential-privacy 库中，把现有的 DP-Adam 或 DP-SGD 训练切换到自动裁剪，只需替换一个函数、并从搜索空间里删掉阈值这一维。对多数使用者而言，这把原本二维的超参搜索变成了一维，而在精度和隐私上都没有可测量的代价。

en.title: NeurIPS 2023 | Removing the Trickiest Knob in Private Deep Learning
en.subtitle: AWS AI and UC Santa Barbara introduce automatic clipping: a one-line replacement that deletes the clipping threshold from any DP optimizer while matching or beating tuned state of the art.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 差分隐私训练里最难调的那个旋钮，其实可以删掉
zh.subtitle: AWS AI 与 UC Santa Barbara 提出自动裁剪（automatic clipping）：一行代码去掉裁剪阈值，效果追平甚至超过精调后的最优基线。

en.text: Why the clipping threshold is such a headache

Standard DP-SGD, following Abadi et al., clips each per-sample gradient g by the factor min(R / ‖g‖, 1): gradients longer than R are scaled down to length R, and shorter ones are left alone. In practice, though, the thresholds that give the best accuracy are tiny, small enough that essentially every per-sample gradient is longer than R and therefore gets clipped at every step. When that happens the min collapses to its first branch, R / ‖g‖, for almost every example. The exact value of R stops carrying any per-example magnitude information; it acts only as a global scale. That observation is the crack the paper pries open.

en.caption: Figure 1. Test accuracy of ResNet18 on ImageNet under DP-SGD, swept over the clipping norm (x-axis) and learning rate (y-axis). Accuracy runs from about 60% at a good configuration down to single digits, and even along a strong learning-rate row it falls sharply once the clipping norm is set too large. The threshold, not just the learning rate, decides the outcome.

en.text: Takeaway

The clipping threshold has been treated as a critical, must-tune knob since DP deep learning began. The message of automatic clipping is that it can simply be removed: normalize each per-sample gradient, add a tiny stability constant, fix the threshold to one, and you are left with an optimizer that is as private, as fast, and as accurate as the best hand-tuned DP methods, backed by a convergence guarantee matching SGD. The honest boundary is that automatic clipping changes how gradients are clipped, not the underlying privacy-utility trade-off of DP itself: noise still has to be added, and very tight privacy budgets are still hard. What it removes is a large, expensive, and largely unnecessary source of friction, which is enough to make private training feel a lot more like ordinary training.

Because the change is a drop-in replacement for the clipping step, it costs almost nothing to try: the authors release it in the open-source fast-differential-privacy library, where switching an existing DP-Adam or DP-SGD run to automatic clipping means swapping one function and deleting the threshold from the search. For most practitioners, that turns a two-dimensional hyperparameter hunt into a one-dimensional one, with no measured cost in accuracy or privacy.

zh.text: 删掉这个旋钮，会牺牲精度吗？不会

最核心的实验，就是要回答一个固定的、无阈值的规则能否真的追平精调过的 R。图3 给出了直接的答案。热力图里每个格子是 RoBERTa-base 在 SST-2、ε = 3 下、某个（裁剪范数，学习率）组合的测试准确率；右侧多出来的 AUTO-S 一列则完全不使用任何调过的阈值。它落在了与最优精调 R 相同的准确率上，也就是说，你只需搜索学习率，整条 R 维度可以直接跳过，调参成本大约省下 5 倍（连同这部分调参本会花掉的隐私预算）。

zh.caption: 图3 RoBERTa-base 在 SST-2 上的测试准确率（DP-Adam，ε = 3），横轴为裁剪阈值 R，纵轴为学习率。红线右侧的 AUTO-S 一列不调阈值，却达到了与最优精调 R 相同的准确率；只搜索学习率，就能把超参网格大约缩小到原来的五分之一。

zh.text: 这个规律在各类任务上都成立，而且往往不只是“追平”，而是明显更好。在图像基准上，相同隐私预算下，AUTO-S 在论文报告的每一个任务上都超过了 Abadi 裁剪，提升最大的地方，正是准确率本来最有空间的任务。

zh.caption: 表1 相同隐私预算 ε 下，AUTO-S 与精调基线的对比。数值为测试准确率（%），越高越好。

zh.text: 语言任务上的结论如出一辙。在 GLUE 的 RoBERTa 微调上，AUTO-S 追平或超过了此前最好的 DP 微调结果；在 GPT2 的 E2E 表格到文本生成上，它拿到了 64.18 的 BLEU（GPT2-large，ε = 3），位居所报告模型的前列。反复出现的主题是：达到这些成绩，方法从不需要一个调过的阈值。
